Notices.text: Part of my work is published and made available as part of the Urban Toolkit, an ecosystem of open-source tools, frameworks, knowledge bases, and methods designed to simplify and accelerate urban data visualization and analysis. For papers, guides, and code, check here.

Prospective students: I am always looking for self-motivated and hard-working PhD students interested in conducting and publishing research. While my work spans a broad range of computer science areas (e.g., machine learning, data management), my primary focus is on visualization and visual analytics. The easiest way to be considered is to apply directly to the PhD program (more info here) and, on your application, indicate your interest in working with me. Depending on factors such as fit and availability, I may then reach out to interview candidates. Please note that I typically do not offer feedback or guidance on admission or supervision before you apply to the program, and I may not be able to respond to all inquiries from prospective students.
